To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we propose the KL-kernel, a novel kernel based on the KL-divergence between Gaussian Markov Processes; 2) we derive the KL kernel for dynamic textures in two forms, one in the image space, one in the hidden state space; 3) we show that the KL-kernel can achieve superior performance over other state-of-the-art methods for dynamic texture classification; 4) we provide experimental results on the KTH and the UMD dynamic texture databases.
we have derived a probabilistic kernel for Gauss-Markov models and we have used the new kernel to build a new classifier that outperforms existing methods.
we have developed a framework for the analysis and classification of visual processes with a probabilistic kernel that is based on the K-L divergence between Gauss-Markow processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a probabilistic kernel for the classification of autoregressive visual processes.
the development of a novel probabilistic kernel for the classification of spatio-temporal processes.
the development of a new framework for the classification and recognition of dynamic visual processes that are modeled as autoregressive models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the new approach is able to classify a large variety of dynamic texture classes, including those with similar appearances but different motions, and those with different appearances and similar motions, while the existing methods can only deal with a limited number of dynamic texture classes.
the KL kernel is a powerful tool in classification tasks where the classes can be modeled as autoregressive processes, and the KL kernel is able to exploit the temporal structure of the data.
this paper presents a new kernel for the classification of autoregressive visual processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have derived a new kernel for dynamic texture classification that is based on the KL-divergence between Gauss-Markoff processes.
we have developed the first kernel-based framework for the classification and recognition of dynamic textures.

we have developed a probabilistic framework for the classification and recognition of visual processes that is based on a new probabilistic model, dynamic texture, and a new probabilistic classifier, the support vector machine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of dynamic textures and the KL-kernel is a powerful framework for the analysis of video data.
probabilistic kernels can be used for video classification and that the resulting classifiers can achieve state-of-the-art performance.
